system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Principal Software Engineer | Backend Systems
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
SUMMARY
Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building large-scale services and
distributed systems in Python, Go and C++. Technical experience includes API development,
high-throughput service design, PostgreSQL and event-driven systems. Led organisations of up to 45
engineers and defined architecture for platforms serving 50M+ users; continue to write code every week,
mostly internal tooling in recent years.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform - Streamhaus GmbH (video streaming), Munich 2019 -
Aug 2026
• Led the platform organisation: 5 teams, 45 engineers and 5 engineering managers, responsible for
identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
• Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE;
improved playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M/year) through rightsizing, committed use discounts and an
internal cost dashboard.
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
• Grew the organisation from 18 to 45 engineers and conducted 200+ interviews.
Principal Engineer - Streamhaus GmbH 2015 - 2019
• Technical lead for the playback API, built with Python, Tornado and later an internal FastAPI-like
framework, Cassandra and Redis.
• Designed an entitlement service handling 120k requests/second at peak using Go and Cassandra.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer - Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart 2010 - 2015
• Developed backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++,
Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led a team of 6 developers on the route-history product.
Software Engineer - Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe 2005 - 2010
• Developed C++ and Python for industrial data acquisition software on Linux and embedded x86.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for 8 years.
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc) Computer Science, Rhine Valley University, 2005
SKILLS
Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI, Tornado, asyncio), Go, C++ (older); PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra,
Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ; GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Terraform;
gRPC, Protobuf; Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry; distributed systems design, architecture
reviews, technical hiring, people management
LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)
PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
• “Running Python at 100k rps” - EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018
• “Cost is a feature” - internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role at Tessel Cargo Software. I bring 21 years
of experience building backend services and distributed systems, with deep experience in Python,
including FastAPI and Tornado, Go, PostgreSQL, APIs and high-throughput platforms. My
earlier work in fleet telematics also gives me direct experience with transport-related systems:
at Nordfels Telematik, I developed backend services ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles.
At Streamhaus, I led the technical development of the playback API and designed a Go
entitlement service handling up to 120,000 requests per second. I later led the platform
organisation through a migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and
Go services, improving playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. Although I have led
engineering organisations, I continue to write code every week and remain motivated by
designing, implementing, and improving backend services. These projects involved building
reliable services at scale and making practical architecture decisions—experience I would bring
to Tessel’s event ingestion and tracking APIs.
Tessel’s focus on reliable shipment visibility, clear design notes and engineers taking ownership
of services aligns well with the way I have worked. I have used PostgreSQL/PostGIS, RabbitMQ
and Kafka, and my experience deploying services on GKE and working with Kubernetes,
Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry would support Tessel’s focus on cloud
operations and observability. I also introduced architecture reviews and on-call guidelines
adopted company-wide, and built a Python test harness that was used by QA for eight years.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend and transport-systems experience
could contribute to Tessel’s Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.
Kind regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
